data.title: Wall Street Bets Billions on Inflation-Era Trades as Oil Tops $100
data.description:
Wall Street is piling into inflation-era trades as oil holds above $100 and inflation remains stubborn, according to Bloomberg.

The bond market also stayed defiant this week, challenging Scott Bessent to bring more policy firepower.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Russia, BRICS Partners Move Toward Space Council
data.description: Russia and its BRICS partners are moving toward creating a council to coordinate cooperation in space, Roscosmos chief Dmitry Bakanov said in an interview in New Delhi, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: CFTC Approves Automatic 30% Whistleblower Awards Under $5 Million
data.description:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission will automatically award successful whistleblowers 30% of enforcement penalties collected when a tipster is due $5 million or less, according to Bloomberg.

The agency said Friday the change is intended to speed payouts for smaller awards.

data.title: Arizona Sues L'Oreal Over Hair Relaxer Cancer Claims
data.description:
According to CNBC, Arizona has sued L'Oreal, accusing the cosmetics company of hiding evidence that its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women. Arizona Attorney General Kristin Mayes filed the lawsuit late Thursday in state court, making Arizona the first state to sue over alleged cancer risks tied to hair relaxers. The complaint says L'Oreal violated state consumer protection laws by marketing the products without warning consumers about alleged risks of ovarian and uterine cancers. Arizona is seeking penalties, damages and a court order that would force L'Oreal to stop selling the products unless it warns of the cancer risk.

The lawsuit comes as L'Oreal faces more than 12,000 similar lawsuits that have been consolidated in a Chicago federal court as part of multidistrict litigation. L'Oreal has said its products undergo rigorous safety reviews and that the claims lack legal or scientific merit. The products have been sold under names including Dark and Lovely and Optimum, and the first lawsuits followed a 2022 National Institutes of Health study that found women who used the products several times a year were more than twice as likely to develop uterine cancer.

data.title: Saudi Foreign Ministry Says East-West Oil Pipeline Hit by Drone Attack From Iraq
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry said the East-West oil pipeline was hit by a drone attack from Iraq and that, at the request of Iraq's prime minister, it is not taking retaliatory action for now, while reserving the right to take all necessary measures to protect its sovereignty, security, facilities, citizens, and residents.

data.title: Bitcoin Traders Shift to Buy-the-Dip as Mark Sishka Warns of Pullback
data.description:
Bitcoin traders have moved from a "sell the rally" stance to "buy the dip" after the asset rallied toward $80,000. According to NS3.AI, Mark Sishka said rebuilt long leverage could still drive a short-term move toward $70,000 to $72,000.

Sishka added that a pullback could form a higher low before Bitcoin makes another attempt at $82,000 to $85,000.

data.description: Firehawk Aerospace is in talks for a private funding round that would value the defense technology company at $1.25 billion, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Stocks End Week Lower as S&P 500 Rises 0.8% on CPI Day
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. stocks ended the week lower, with the S&P 500 down 0.4%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 1.5%, and the Nasdaq down 0.5%; on Friday, when U.S. CPI inflation data was released, the S&P 500 initially rose 0.8%, the Nasdaq 100 was roughly flat, and several Nasdaq 100 components moved higher, including ADI up 4.7%, NXP up 4.5%, Cisco up 4.3%, Texas Instruments up 3.7%, Qualcomm up 2.8%, Intel up 2.6%, SpaceX up 2.2%, Google A up 1.9%, and Apple up 1.8%, while Nebius Group fell 1.6%, Palo Alto Networks fell 2.3%, Western Digital fell 3%, SanDisk fell 3.6%, and Seagate Technology fell 3.7%.

data.title: U.S. Central Command Says U.S. Forces Continue Maritime Blockade Operations Against Iran
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. Central Command said U.S. forces continued maritime blockade operations against Iran and had caused 99 merchant ships to change course as of September 11.

data.title: US Dollar Holds Steady After CPI Data Briefly Pushes It to Intraday High
data.description:
The dollar gave back gains on Friday after data showed U.S. core consumer prices rose more than expected, prompting traders to increase bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike next week. According to Sina Finance, the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index was little changed after touching an intraday high following the inflation release.

A key U.S. consumer price gauge rose more than expected last month, reinforcing the case for a rate increase by Fed officials next week. More Wall Street firms, including TD Securities and MUFG, have begun backing the view that a near-term hike is likely, while swap traders now see about a 90% chance of a rate increase at next week’s Fed meeting.

Economists expect the Bank of Japan to raise its benchmark rate next week and to hike again by January, with policy normalization likely to accelerate. USD/CAD rose 0.2% to 1.3863, while EUR/USD fell 0.1% to 1.1599 and GBP/USD rose 0.1% to 1.3528.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Finalizes Anti-Dumping and Countervailing Duties on Solar Products From India, Indonesia, and Laos
data.description: According to Sina Finance, the U.S. Department of Commerce issued final determinations finding that solar products produced in India, Indonesia, and Laos benefited from unfair subsidies. India’s dumping margin was set at 123.04%, with countervailing duties of 126.09%; Indonesia’s dumping margin was set at 94.36%, with countervailing duties ranging from 73.2% to 173.7%; and Laos’ dumping margin was 65.43%, with countervailing duties ranging from 82.03% to 153.67%.

data.title: Unifor Says Talks With Stellantis Stall Over Brampton Plant
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Unifor said talks with Stellantis have stalled, and it rejected a deal in the absence of a solution for the Brampton plant. Stellantis will sell the Brampton plant to Roshel.

data.title: CFTC: Speculators Cut Net Short Positions in CBOT 5-Year and 10-Year Treasury Futures
data.description: According to Jin10, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said that for the week ended September 8, 2026, speculators cut net short positions in CBOT 5-year U.S. Treasury futures by 113,020 contracts to 1,267,493 contracts, and reduced net short positions in CBOT 10-year U.S. Treasury futures by 74,492 contracts to 834,783 contracts.

data.title: Fund Managers Cut S&P 500 Futures Net Longs To Weekly Low, CFTC Says
data.description: U.S. fund managers reduced their net long positions in S&P 500 futures to the lowest level of the past week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said. According to ChainCatcher, the report indicates a pullback in bullish positioning on the index futures market.

data.title: STOCKS | ICE Dollar Index Rises 0.07% as U.S. CPI Triggers Sharp Intraday Swing
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the ICE U.S. dollar index rose 0.07% to 99.118 in New York late trading on Friday, September 11, briefly spiking and then reversing after the U.S. CPI inflation data was released at 20:30 (UTC+8), ending the week roughly flat with a trading range of 1184.82-1192.98 and a V-shaped pattern that set a period high at the time of the CPI release. The Bloomberg Dollar Index fell 0.02% to 1190.45, down 0.02% for the week and also trading between 1184.82 and 1192.98.

data.title: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Says Saudi Arabia, Japan, and Jordan Will Face Consequences
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Saudi Arabia, Japan, and Jordan will face consequences for supporting an International Atomic Energy Agency resolution against Iran.
